author_or_org: Ha Jeong Kim, Saksonita Khoeurn, Ye Ji Yoon

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper describes a semantic-layer-mediated NL2SQL agent that separates semantic intent from physical SQL execution by having the agent reason over a curated semantic layer via a compact intermediate representation called the Semantic Model Query (SMQ), instead of generating SQL directly over raw schemas.
claims.quote: We present a semantic-layer-mediated NL2SQL agent that decouples semantic intent from physical SQL execution. Rather than generating SQL directly over raw schemas, the agent reasons over a curated semantic layer through a compact intermediate representation called the Semantic Model Query (SMQ).

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A deterministic compiler translates each SMQ into dialect-specific SQL, producing verified building blocks that the agent composes into the final query.
claims.quote: A deterministic compiler translates each SMQ into dialect-specific SQL, providing verified building blocks that the agent composes into the final query.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Using Gemini 3 Pro, the system achieves 94.15% execution accuracy on the 547-task Spider2-snow benchmark, ranks third on the official leaderboard, and substantially outperforms schema-only approaches.
claims.quote: Using Gemini 3 Pro, the system achieves 94.15% execution accuracy on the 547-task Spider2-snow benchmark, ranking third on the official leaderboard and substantially outperforming schema-only approaches.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The system supports SQLite, BigQuery, and Snowflake backends and is integrated into an end-to-end evaluation framework.
claims.quote: The system employs a constrained think-act loop, supports SQLite, BigQuery, and Snowflake backends, and is integrated into an end-to-end evaluation framework.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper discusses semantic-layer quality and the trade-off between improved grounding and overfitting.
claims.quote: We describe the system architecture, SMQ representation, agent workflow, evaluation results, and discuss semantic-layer quality and the trade-off between improved grounding and overfitting.
